claims.kill_rule: One NOT-SUPPORTED verdict on any of the 47 cited ids from any declared seat, an id with fewer than 2 counted SUPPORTED seats, or any other leg FAIL, fails the claim. The judged object is the entry whose sha256 the packet key records; after the support task call no byte of the entry, of SOURCES rows S600-S651 or of the captures changes before the final measure. A miss is reported, never amended, narrowed or re-scaled; no row or line is removed after a verdict.
claims.fetch_rule: FETCH-60: no ACCEPT-D-60 leg fetches over the network. PINNED reads committed captures only. A support reviewer opens each page by its listed live URL or its listed Wayback capture; a page the reviewer cannot open by any listed URL is answered NOT-SUPPORTED (reason: unreachable), which fails the claim. This treatment is frozen here and never relaxed.
review_only: whether each repaired sentence is the best wording a scholar would choose

PROVENANCE beyond the leg: that each session file ~/.omp/agent/sessions/*/*/KotodamaR60/KotodamaR60.<Seat>.jsonl is the one omp wrote for that dispatched seat (the closure compares it with history://KotodamaR60.<Seat>); the leg itself requires each committed transcript to be a byte copy of that session file
planted-rows.sha256 committed before the first data seat; planted-key.sha256 committed before the support task call (git log of both)
controls_before_data: do-nothing: the claim base, and the base plus records only
junk: lines and rows citing S648-S651 with junk text, junk captures, fabricated support files
all-false and all-true reviewers (every verdict NOT-SUPPORTED; every verdict SUPPORTED)
no-reader: reports without packets or transcripts; a transcript with no fetch of the row's page
shortcut keyed on ids or labels: a reviewer keyed on packet labels or on the lane's committed registry/entry (reads the lane instead of the pages)
post-verdict narrowing (the round-59 shape): drop rows or lines after the verdicts
old wording: the round-59 rejected sentences restored with the new ids
server echo / self-made capture: a capture or URL that echoes the quote
